# General Information {#general-information}

## Welcome {#welcome}

The Funding Committee (FunCom) has prepared this guide to help graduate students and graduate registered student groups (GRSOs) understand and apply for Graduate Assembly (GA) funding and other resources. The guide details application requirements and lays out the responsibilities expected of groups if they receive funding. Individuals and GRSOs must read the Funding Guide, review it, and use it as a reference tool when requesting funds from the GA and when submitting purchase requests.

## Land Acknowledgement {#land-acknowledgement}

The Graduate Assembly recognizes that UC Berkeley sits on the territory of xučyun (Huichin), the ancestral and unceded land of the Chochenyo speaking Ohlone people, the successors of the sovereign Verona Band of Alameda County. This land was and continues to be of great importance to the Muwekma Ohlone Tribe and other familial descendants of the Verona Band.

We recognize that every member of the Berkeley community has, and continues to benefit from, the use and occupation of this land, since the institution’s founding in 1868\. Consistent with the GA’s values, we have a responsibility to acknowledge and make visible the university’s relationship to Native peoples. As members of the Berkeley community, it is vitally important that we not only recognize the history of the land on which we stand, but also, we recognize that the Muwekma Ohlone people are alive and flourishing members of the Berkeley and broader Bay Area communities today.

## What is the Graduate Assembly? {#what-is-the-graduate-assembly?}

The Graduate Assembly (GA) is the official representative body of the graduate and professional students at the University of California, Berkeley (UCB). The fundamental principles of the GA are the promotion of a vibrant student social life, inclusiveness, activism, community service, educational improvement, and professional development. In service to these principles the GA advocates for students, funds graduate and professional student groups on campus, provides travel grants, and directly manages a variety of projects. You can learn more about the Graduate Assembly at [their website](https://ga.berkeley.edu/about/).

# So You Want Funding? A Quick Guide {#so-you-want-funding?-a-quick-guide}

In general, you apply for funding at [the GA Funding CalLink page](https://callink.berkeley.edu/organization/gafunding). All non-exhausted funding sources will have the forms linked from there.

If you’re an **individual** looking for funds for individual activities, like conference travel, you want one of our individual awards. There are two: one for general professional development, and one for expenses related to children when traveling for academic purposes (either traveling with a child or finding childcare at home). Both have a quick application process. The Professional Development Award requires an email from a member of the faculty confirming your plans and telling us that they are for your professional development. We do not need a whole letter of recommendation, nor will we consider one if we receive one. You might also consider the [Mutual Aid Fund](https://ga.berkeley.edu/ga-resources/ga-scholarships-and-grants/graduate-assembly-mutual-aid-fund/), which this guide does not cover.

If you’re a **group**, or you want to plan **group activities**, either you’re a registered GRSO or you aren’t. If you aren’t, we can’t fund you as a group, but we can fund an individual organizer who makes all the purchases and runs the event through Independent Organizer Funding. You can apply for this every month, with a total cap of $1000 per semester. If you are a GRSO, you can either apply for large-project funding up to $2000 once at the beginning of every semester, or up to $500 in every month’s funding round, until you hit a total cap of $2000 for the semester. 

**Note: While $2000 is the maximum amount of funding available to any GRSO, funds are distributed at the discretion of the funding committee and funding caps may be lowered based on demand. We recommend that you budget for at most $1000 \- $1500 in GA funding each semester.**  

The Graduate Assembly encourages GRSOs to serve plant-based meals. When you apply for GRSO funding, you will be given the option to self-certify as a plant-based GRSO. Specifically, this means that you are serving a full meal – not just snacks – at at least one event for which you are applying for funding in this round, and that you commit to serving only plant-based food at any event for which you are applying for funding in this round. A meal with a meat and a vegetarian option does not qualify. There is a further fund of money for plant-based GRSOs, which will be used to increase your funding at the discretion of the Funding Officer and FunCom. (At the time of writing, the GA is applying for money to fill this fund; it may turn out to contain a total of $0. Should you have questions about the current status of the fund, contact the Funding Officer.)

To apply for group funding, fill out the relevant form on the CalLink page. You’ll need the following:

* A sponsoring delegate. This can be any GA delegate, although, if your department has one, we recommend you ask them. There is a [delegate directory](https://ga.berkeley.edu/for-delegates/delegate-directory/) on the GA website.

* A budget, listing all your planned purchases, including estimated attendance for events. Remember that you can spend up to $20 per graduate student attendee per event on food, and $1 per non-graduate-student attendee. In general, we recommend you use our [budget template](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1bQmbQ47Qqy_zqRi4oJLLALhAfaHbhl36gAWa-ZUSvk4/copy).

You will also need to complete the funding quiz. This can be accessed from the application form. **You must get a perfect score on the funding quiz before you apply. The Funding Committee checks this for every application, and never, under any circumstances, recommends GRSO or Independent Organizer funding for an application that comes from someone who has not passed that year’s funding quiz.** You can see your score after completing the quiz by clicking on the “View score” button. Applicants for the Professional Development and Graduate Parent Travel Awards do not need to complete the funding quiz.

Fill out the application by the deadline on the [calendar](#the-funding-calendar). If you applied for a Professional Development or Graduate Parent Travel Award, you will hear back by the decision date and the process is complete. If you applied for GRSO or Independent Organizer Funding, your application is then considered by the Funding Committee, which then sends you and your sponsoring delegate a tentative recommendation. If you are unhappy with that recommendation, you can appeal; details for the appeal are given along with the tentative recommendation, but deadlines are often tight, so be prepared. The Funding Appeals Board meets a few days before the deadline to consider appeals, and its decisions are the final recommendations given to the Delegate Assembly. At its monthly meeting, the Assembly has the opportunity to amend the recommendations in any way it wishes – your sponsoring delegate may be useful here – and then approves them, at which point you receive your funding.

Your funding may come with other conditions. In particular, GRSO Large-Project Funding requires that your event be advertised through GA channels and that any promotional materials specifically mention the GA. [See the section on advertising for more information.](#advertising-and-accessibility)

There is very high demand for GRSO funding throughout the year, and you may well not receive all the money you request. We really do try to fund everyone we can to the greatest extent possible, and we are putting in a lot of work to seek out extra funding sources. Be assured we don’t like it any more than you do.

![A flowchart summarizing the information in this section on how to choose the funding program that best meets your needs.][image2]

| Group funding checklist | Individual funding checklist |
| ----- | ----- |
| A sponsoring GA delegate A budget (we have a [template](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1bQmbQ47Qqy_zqRi4oJLLALhAfaHbhl36gAWa-ZUSvk4/copy)) A description of the planned event or project A score of 100% on the funding quiz | For PD award only: a short email from a faculty member A description of the planned event, conference, or project Eligibility (Ph.D. students twice per award, everyone else once) |

# Funding Authority {#funding-authority}

## Funding Committee {#funding-committee}

The Funding Committee (FunCom) has the authority to recommend which graduate student groups shall be eligible for funding, to recommend funding allocations for each application, and to recommend funding sources subject to the restrictions herein. These recommendations are provided to the Delegate Assembly for final approval. In accordance with applicable Federal and State law and University policy, the GA prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, physical or mental disability, age, medical condition (cancer-related or genetic characteristics), ancestry, marital status, age, sexual orientation, or status as a covered veteran (special disabled veteran, Vietnam-era veteran, or any other veteran who served on active duty during a war or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized). This nondiscrimination policy covers admission, access, and treatment in GA programs, funding, and activities. In addition, receiving GA funding previously does **not** guarantee funding in the current or future rounds. Both GRSO and Independent Organizer Funding application evaluations are subjective and merit-based, and final allocation of funds is left to the discretion of the GA delegate body. 

## Funding Appeals Board {#funding-appeals-board}

If a student organization disagrees with the funding recommendation of the Funding Committee, they may appeal the decision to the Funding Appeals Board, which has the authority to modify recommendations given by the Funding Committee. This committee is convened by the Internal Vice President and consists of the Internal Vice President, the Vice President of Finance, the Rules Officer, and the Funding Officer or their designee. Appeals must be e-mailed to the Funding Officer and the Internal Vice President after notification of the Funding Committee's decision and prior to delegate approval. Appeals must contain the specific decision being appealed and the reasons for the appeal.

## Funding Officer {#funding-officer}

The GA Funding Officer has the authority to grant any changes to events that have been allocated GA money, including but not limited to changes to event dates, speakers, venue, location, food costs, and supply costs. However, only the delegate body can approve an overall increase in the amount of money allocated to any given organization or person.

## Delegate Body Authority with respect to GA Funding {#delegate-body-authority-with-respect-to-ga-funding}

**The delegate body has ultimate authority and final decision for approving and/or modifying all FunCom funding recommendations for all categories**. The delegate body holds the Funding Committee accountable to adhere to all the policies set forth in this guide. As stated above, the final allocation of GA funds for any application is left to the discretion of the GA delegate body. If a delegate wishes to amend the FunCom funding recommendations, they should motion to do so at the delegates meeting in which the funding application of interest is being approved. If an applicant wishes to amend the FunCom funding recommendations and is not a delegate, they should contact their sponsoring delegate to advocate on their behalf. Once the delegate body approves funding allocations, the decision is final and future motions cannot change the approved funding.

The GA runs a funding round every month during the academic year. GRSO Large-Project Funding is only available during the Summer, September, and January rounds; all other funding is considered every month.

All funding awarded in the Summer through the November and December funding rounds must be used by December 31, 2026, after which point it will be reclaimed by the Graduate Assembly and reallocated. All funding awarded in the January through June funding rounds must be used by June 30, 2027\. The GA funds the future, not the past.

All receipts are due thirty days after the date of the event or by the end of the semester (December 31 or June 30), whichever comes first.

|   | GRSO Large-Project Funding | GRSO Continuing Funding | Independent Organizer Funding |

| **Period of utilization** | Until the end of the semester in which the award is given | Until the end of the semester in which the award is given | Until the end of the academic year in which the award is given |

## GRSO Large-Project Funding {#grso-large-project-funding}

Large-Project Funding provides financial support for specific, large projects that form the centerpieces of GRSOs’ semesters and years. To qualify for GRSO Large-Project Funding, projects must have a justified budget of more than $500, which is to be spent during or in preparation for at most two days’ worth of events. Exceptions to this rule can be granted by the Funding Committee, and the application will have a space to request such an exception.

Applications for Large-Project Funding will be considered once in the summer, once in the fall semester, and once in the spring. No exceptions will be made.

For large events, GRSOs should consider applying to other campus funds, such as:

* [Wellness Fund](https://wellnessfund.berkeley.edu/apply-funds)

* [TGIF: The Green Initiative Fund](https://tgif.berkeley.edu/grants/#1533660590626-5e404470-85c5)

* [CACSSF](https://studentaffairs.berkeley.edu/about/vice-chancellor/chancellors-advisory-committee-on-student-services-and-fees-cacssf/funding-requests/)

* [Chancellor's Community Partnership Fund](https://chancellor.berkeley.edu/gcr/local-community/programs-initiatives/ccpf)

## GRSO Continuing Funding {#grso-continuing-funding}

Continuing Funding provides financial support for meetings, events, and the general operations of a GRSO. Applications will be considered once a month during the academic year, and once at the end of the academic year in preparation for the summer. Continuing Funding will usually only fund events during the funding month following the application; in other words, if you want to host an event in October 2 \- November 5, we won’t fund you until the funding round immediately preceding October. Funding may also be awarded for events very early in the next funding round that would be difficult to cancel if funding were not awarded, although this is not guaranteed.

## Funding for Plant-Based GRSOs {#funding-for-plant-based-grsos}

When applying for GRSO funding of any kind, a GRSO may self-certify as plant-based if both of the following are true:

* At least one event being applied for in the current funding round includes a full meal, and  
* All meals, snacks, and other food served at all events being applied for in the current funding round will be fully plant-based. (Specifically, the Graduate Assembly defines meat as “the tissue of a deceased animal”; a meal is considered fully plant-based if it includes no meat. A meal with a vegetarian option and a meat option does not qualify.)

The GA has established a secondary pot of money to increase the amount of funding allocated to GRSOs which self-certify in this way. (This money was granted by organizations which promote climate-conscious purchases, not drawn from the general GRSO fund.) For more information on the current status of the fund, or on the status of GRSO funding in general, contact the Funding Officer at [funding@ga.berkeley.edu](mailto:funding@ga.berkeley.edu).

GRSOs that self-certify as plant-based are subject to added scrutiny, and may at any point be asked to provide proof, such as itemized receipts or photographs of events, that they are indeed serving only plant-based food. An intentional purchase of meat by a self-certified plant-based GRSO is grounds for revocation of all GA funding granted to that GRSO, not just the extra funding granted from the secondary pot. Should you realize that you have accidentally purchased meat on behalf of a plant-based GRSO, contact the Funding Officer immediately at [funding@ga.berkeley.edu](mailto:funding@ga.berkeley.edu). In this scenario, it is far less likely that your funding will be revoked.

## Restrictions on GRSO Funding In General {#restrictions-on-grso-funding-in-general}

Applications are merit-based, and the Funding Committee has the discretion to fund any application in full, partially, or not at all.

**Any events allocated money from the Graduate Assembly must be open, available, and advertised for attendance to any graduate or professional student at the University of California, Berkeley.**

### **Maximum Funding** {#maximum-funding}

* A GRSO can apply for up to $2000 per Large-Project round or $500 per Continuing round, to a total of $2000 per semester across all rounds for both types of funding. In practice, the Graduate Assembly does not always have sufficient funds to give all GRSOs the full $2000, and we recommend that GRSOs not expect more than $1000 \- $1500 per semester and perhaps less.

* In each round, the total spending for each event, including food, is limited to $20/graduate or professional student expected attendee and $1/any other expected attendee.

  * An event with a meeting of 10 graduate students and 3 undergraduates can be funded to a maximum of $203.

* GRSOs may request reasonable exceptions to the maximum funding caps. You must submit a justification in your application to receive an exception. Exceptions will be granted at the Funding Committee’s discretion. Examples of reasonable exceptions include:

  * A multi-day event which requires funding exceeding the per-attendee cap.

  * An event where building reservation fees or honoraria exceed the funding cap.

* **The Funding Committee always has the discretion to make exceptions to any caps, and to recommend funding any application in full, partially, or not at all. Further caps may be imposed at any time in order to ensure equitable distribution of funds.**

### **Funding Utilization** {#funding-utilization}

When you apply for GRSO Funding, you must state if you applied for and received funding from any previous rounds that semester. If you submit an application and have used less than 50% of your previously allocated funding, you must submit a justification in your application. If there is not a justification submitted, FunCom may choose to not recommend your application for funding that round.

### **Other Sources of GRSO Funding** {#other-sources-of-grso-funding}

The Funding Committee and Officer may consider what other non-GA funding sources a GRSO has access to in their CalLink accounts in making recommended funding allocations.

### **Sponsoring Delegates** {#sponsoring-delegates}

A GRSO must identify a sponsoring delegate to represent them to be eligible for GRSO Funding.

### **Spending Timelines** {#spending-timelines}

**Allocations must be spent within the academic semester and any unused allocations by the end of the semester will be reclaimed by the GA.** In other words, funding allocations do not rollover between semesters or academic years.

The GA funds the future, not the past. No GRSO may apply for money to cover the cost of an event that will take place before the date the funding will be approved.

## Independent Organizer Funding {#independent-organizer-funding}

Independent Organizer Funding provides funds for people who wish to organize events or generally make the world a better place but do not have the structure of a GRSO. DEI events are often a focus of Independent Organizer Funding, as are events held by people who are considering starting a GRSO but have not yet formally formed a group.

Any graduate or professional student may apply for Independent Organizer Funding during the same rounds for which GRSOs apply for Continuing Funding. The cap is $1000 per semester per applicant, although **the Funding Committee has the discretion to fund any application in full, partially, or not at all, and may impose further caps in order to impose an equitable distribution of funds.** The $20 per graduate or professional student and $1 per other attendee restriction from GRSO Funding also applies here.

As part of the application for Independent Organizer Funding, the applicant will be required to justify why they cannot fund their plans through GRSO Funding of some sort instead.

Applications will be reviewed for feasibility and merit by the Funding Committee. Individual projects funded in full by the GA will not exceed $1,000 per project. Groups may request funding in excess of this amount if they plan to secure matching dollars from other sources (such as the [Dean’s Graduate Diversity Innovation Fund](https://grad.berkeley.edu/graduate-diversity/current-grad-students/deans-graduate-diversity-innovation-fund/)) for all funds allocated beyond this full funding cap. Applicants needn’t have already secured matching funds to receive an award in excess of $1000, but should provide information about the funds they are pursuing. Funds in excess of $1000 will be disbursed by the GA when proof of matching dollars has been received.

# Funding Awards for Individuals {#funding-awards-for-individuals}

## Professional Development Award {#professional-development-award}

The mission of the Graduate Assembly is to improve the lives and outcomes of all graduate and professional students. Student funding through the Professional Development Award is meant to improve the lives of students in all programs and stages from first years to students in their final stages at Berkeley. Professional development needs and available resources vary between academic programs and the needs of all graduate and professional students may vary significantly.

The scope of the Professional Development Award covers all professional development activity including, but not limited to:

1. Later-stage students, particularly students completing exams and dissertations, who would benefit from external academic and writing coaching,

2. Students without other funding who would benefit from travel to conferences in their fields,

3. Students who wish to purchase software or equipment necessary for their work that their department is not able to provide, and

4. Students wishing to gain professional skills outside of their academic research focus, such as by taking classes or attending conferences.

The application process for the Professional Development Award includes a requirement that the applicant justify the merit of the professional development activity being applied for and demonstrate that existing departmental and university resources do not provide sufficient support for such activities.

Any graduate student can obtain up to $500 from this award within any given year; awards will generally be for this amount. Students in a PhD program are eligible to receive this award twice throughout their time at Berkeley, while students in a Master’s or equivalent professional program will only be eligible once.

**The applicant’s sponsoring professor or advisor must email the [Funding Officer](mailto:funding@ga.berkeley.edu) from an @berkeley.edu academic email address stating that the conference benefits the student’s educational or research endeavors. A long letter is not required.**

## Graduate Student Parent Travel Award {#graduate-student-parent-travel-award}

The GA also recognizes the special needs of graduate student parents to attend conferences and/or seminars while also filling the needs of their family and children. Campus does not currently offer funding support for graduate student parents to curb the additional costs associated with travel for children and/or a caregiver to conferences outside of the Bay Area or for childcare at such conferences. As such, the GA has established the Graduate Student Parent (GSP) Travel Award to aid with such expenses. 

The GSP Travel Award provides funding for graduate student parents or legal guardians who, out of necessity, must bring their child(ren)/minor dependent and/or a caregiver for their child(ren) to conferences outside of the San Francisco Bay Area. Funds from this award may be used for travel costs for children or a caregiver or for other childcare needed for the student parent to attend conferences. There are no presentation requirements for the graduate student parent associated with this award, but priority will be given to graduate student parents who will be presenting. Additionally, this award does not require Academic Advisor or program advisor approval, to ensure student parents are not unfairly discriminated against. Graduate student parents may be eligible for both the Professional Development Award and GSP Travel Award.

Any graduate student can obtain up to $500 from this award within any given year; awards will generally be for this amount. Students in a PhD program are eligible to receive this award twice throughout their time at Berkeley, while students in a Master’s or equivalent professional program will only be eligible once.

## Policies for PD and GSP Travel Awards {#policies-for-pd-and-gsp-travel-awards}

The selection process for both awards is merit blind. If applications exceed available funding, funding will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis . The GA will allocate approximately half of the Professional Development Award and Graduate Student Parent (GSP) Travel Award in the fall, and half in the spring. Awards will be granted on a rolling basis until funds are exhausted. Graduate student parents may apply for both awards.

This award is allocated via purchase reimbursements. Awardees will not receive the award in a lump sum but will need to submit receipts for reimbursement. For all award reimbursements, you will need to submit a Purchase Request (PR) on the GA Travel Awards CalLink page within 30 days of the professional development activity. Maximums for expenses are set by the UC Berkeley travel policy.

Only currently registered full-time graduate students or students on filing fee during the semester in which the activity/conference will occur may apply for and receive a Professional Development Award or GSP Travel Award. 

Funding support for the GA Professional Development Award is provided as part of the Peet’s Student Support Program. A portion of every Peet's Coffee purchase made at Cal Dining Peet's locations helps support student programs and initiatives including graduate travel grants, student scholarships, campus sustainability programs, a basic needs skills course, and an on-campus farm and gardening program. Visit the Peet's partner page to learn more.

The PD and GSP applications do not open and close every month in the same way that GRSO and Independent Organizer funding applications do, but the awards work on the same calendar. Applications submitted by the funding deadline for every month will be considered that month, and notifications will be sent out by the notification date.

All individual awards are the sole prerogative of the Funding Officer. No appeal is possible.

# Funding Policies and Restrictions {#funding-policies-and-restrictions}

Most GA awards are funded by student fees paid each semester by graduate students. Therefore, the GA and all individuals and groups funded by the GA must abide by the rules and restrictions that govern the use of student fee dollars.

## Specifically Forbidden Uses of GA Funding of Any Kind {#specifically-forbidden-uses-of-ga-funding-of-any-kind}

* Funding for events aimed only at select members of a group (board meetings, senior team retreats, and the like) rather than open to all members of the group or to the UC Berkeley community as a whole  
* Snacks or decorations for club offices that are not associated with specific events  
* Any event associated with one particular class year  
* Any gifts, for individuals or groups, or gift cards  
* Prizes (from raffles, etc.)  
* Scholarships or fellowships  
* Bottled water  
* Non-compostable, disposable cutlery  
* Weapons or illegal substances   
* Alcohol. Religious exemptions may be considered by emailing the GA Vice President of Finance [budget@ga.berkeley.edu](mailto:budget@ga.berkeley.edu) and the GA Funding Officer [funding@ga.berkeley.edu](mailto:funding@ga.berkeley.edu).  
* Salaries or regular, periodic stipends  
* T-shirts or other apparel  
* Direct contributions to political campaigns  
* Fixed capital expenditures or durable goods, such as office equipment or books, in excess of $500  
* Software purchases (outside of the Professional Development Award)  
* Logoed items, including banners and large posters  
* Customized club gear, such as bags, pencils, or USB hubs  
* Travel or lodging expenses for individuals (outside of the Professional Development Award, GSP Travel Award, or Honoraria)  
* Website hosting or creation  
* Intramural fees  
* Lodging or transportation costs for off-campus and/or overnight events/retreats

## Location restrictions {#location-restrictions}

* All projects, events, and meetings must generally be held on campus – which includes University Village and Richmond Field Station – or within a 2-mile radius from the edge of main campus (specifically, the area which the UC officially calls the Campus Park). This restriction ensures that all GA-funded events are accessible to all graduate and professional students. Exemptions to this policy are very rarely granted. [An interactive map of this area is available here](https://cal.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/basic/index.html?appid=75e8aed29db147558d15a1cb4a4f33e2), and a static map is available in the [Appendix](#appendix:-acceptable-locations-for-ga-sponsored-events).

* If a project, meeting, or event must take place outside of this area, the applicant must provide the following:

  * Thorough justification of the need for an off-campus location, including an explanation of why available resources within the university are insufficient,

  * An explanation of how free or subsidized transportation will be provided to any interested graduate or professional student to attend, and

  * A note of the distance (in miles) to campus.

* Venue rentals costing more than $800 are likely to not be funded in full. Please search for rentals on campus or nearby that are free or less than $800. 

* Note that Anthony Hall is available to graduate students free of charge, including custodial fees. If Event Services attempt to charge for an event in Anthony Hall, contact the GA President immediately at [president@ga.berkeley.edu](mailto:president@ga.berkeley.edu).

## Advertising and Accessibility {#advertising-and-accessibility}

* The following are mandatory for events granted Large-Project Funding, and highly encouraged for other kinds of events:

  * Posting your event to the GA Events Calendar at [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdmfqLgFiTf4S4rSsXkoDpw-vYxsr8rTzNkdr4i1RkwZneXpQ/viewform?usp=header](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdmfqLgFiTf4S4rSsXkoDpw-vYxsr8rTzNkdr4i1RkwZneXpQ/viewform?usp=header)**,**

  * Submitting your event to the GA Delegates’ Digest via email to [gacommunications@berkeley.edu](mailto:gacommunications@berkeley.edu),

  * Mentioning on all advertising materials that the event is sponsored by the UCB Graduate Assembly, and

  * Including the following text on advertising material:

    * *Event is ADA accessible. For disability accommodation requests and information, please contact Disability Access Services by phone at 510.643.6456 (voice) or 510.642.6376 (TTY) or by email at accessibility@berkeley.edu.*

* Any GA-funded event must be open to all UCB graduate students and should be free of a mandatory charge. **If an entrance or participation fee must be charged, the applicant must justify this fee in the application.**

## Honoraria {#honoraria}

* From the [campus Honoraria Guidelines](https://controller.berkeley.edu/financial-operations/accounts-payable/honoraria-guidelines): “An honorarium is normally a one-time payment granted in recognition of a special service or distinguished achievement for which propriety precludes setting a fixed price, such as a special lecture, participation in a workshop or panel discussion, or similar activities. If the fee is prescribed by the individual or if it is negotiated, an honorarium situation does not exist, rather a contract for services exists \[*sic*\].”

* Both monetary payments and reimbursements for travel costs, including airfare, hotel fees, taxi fees, car rentals, and parking passes, are considered honoraria.

* Funds for guest travel must follow the limits set by campus policy.

* Applicants are required to include a brief bio of the speaker(s) in their funding application.

* GRSOs must abide by the funding caps described by the [Honoraria Guidelines](https://controller.berkeley.edu/financial-operations/accounts-payable/honoraria-guidelines) (but do not need to request approvals as the Guidelines dictate), as well as the limits of the GA funding round being used.

* To ensure equitable distribution of funds across GRSOs, an honorarium may not exceed $500 per awardee per day, counting travel days, unless itemized travel expenses are provided for reimbursement in excess of $500. Larger honoraria may be approved in rare circumstances when the GRSO has secured matching funds from another organization or funding source, and the honorarium recipient and amount is approved in advance by the GA.

* Honorarium payments are made through ASUC Finance, not directly by individual GRSO members.  Submit a purchase request, using the same form as if you were requesting reimbursement, but instead of a receipt submit a [Payment Voucher](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a6I4x3BlIutMQC3vtjBGdj7RU0Tj9YD0/view?usp=sharing). More details are available in the Finance Agent training; your GRSO should have at least two Finance Agents. Contact ASUC Finance at [asucfinance@berkeley.edu](mailto:asucfinance@berkeley.edu) with any questions.

* **No payment can be made with cash or check(s) drawn on a student’s personal account, gift cards, or similar purchases in lieu of a Payment Voucher due to tax reporting requirements. Such expenditures will not be reimbursed by the Graduate Assembly.**

## Student Services and Payment Vouchers {#student-services-and-payment-vouchers}

* GRSOs can pay graduate students, other members of the campus community, and individuals unaffiliated with campus for work and services provided to the GRSO. Contracted services include payment for all efforts and services rendered, including any preparations, travel, or other services billed at either a flat or hourly/daily rate. 

  * All contractors providing services must supply GRSOs with an invoice detailing the services rendered and associated costs. Services should be specific and tied to a particular GRSO event or activity. Salaries or regular, periodic stipends are not reimbursable with GA funds.

  * If a GRSO wishes to pay a GRSO member or another UCB graduate student for a contracted service, the service provider should have prior experience providing the service in question to others in a professional capacity. For example, a GRSO member who regularly teaches paid exercise classes may provide an exercise class as a contracted service for the GRSO, but if they have only led such activities for friends or in other informal settings, a contracted service payment would not be appropriate. GRSOs may not use a contracted service to compensate GRSO members just for organizing or participating in the activities of the GRSO.

* Any agreement for payment when the fee is stipulated or negotiated by the payee is a contracted service (as opposed to an honorarium, above). 

* To ensure equitable distribution of funds across GRSOs, a contracted service payment may not exceed $500 per day of work performed, or $500 per service rendered, whichever is higher. When the invoice is billed hourly, payment shall not exceed $500 per 8 hours of work performed, or $500 per service rendered, whichever is higher. Larger contracted service payments may be approved in rare circumstances when the GRSO has secured matching funds from another organization or funding source, and the honorarium recipient and amount is approved in advance by the GA.

* Payments are made for contracted services through ASUC Finance, not directly by individual GRSO members.  Submit a purchase request, using the same form as if you were requesting reimbursement, but instead of a receipt submit a [Payment Voucher](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a6I4x3BlIutMQC3vtjBGdj7RU0Tj9YD0/view?usp=sharing). More details are available in the Finance Agent training; your GRSO should have at least two Finance Agents. Contact ASUC Finance at [asucfinance@berkeley.edu](mailto:asucfinance@berkeley.edu) with any questions.

* **No payment can be made with cash or check(s) drawn on a student’s personal account, gift cards or similar purchases in lieu of a Payment Voucher due to tax reporting requirements. Such expenditures will not be reimbursed by the Graduate Assembly.**

## Food {#food}

* The GA allocates funds for food and beverages at GRSO events and meetings based on a $20.00 per UC Berkeley graduate student and $1.00 per other attendee up to the application cap for each round, regardless of the number of meals during the event.

* The cap is per-event, not per-meal, and includes snacks. If your event will last multiple days, an exception to the cap may be made at the Funding Committee’s discretion. Provide an explanation in your application.

* In keeping with the GA’s commitment to sustainability, the GA does not provide funding for bottled water or non-compostable disposable cutlery at campus events.

* Multiple GRSOs **cannot** apply to fund the same event for food.

* If you end up with large amounts of leftover food, please consider donating it to [a local food recovery program](https://resource.stopwaste.org/food-recovery-organizations).

* GRSOs are encouraged, but not required, to purchase from small local businesses.

## Resources and Equipment {#resources-and-equipment}

* Students can borrow audio/visual equipment and common office supplies from the GA office (Eshleman 444). In general, GRSOs should attempt to minimize costs by borrowing or sharing supplies and resources with the GA or other GRSOs. Contact the GA Business Office for more information.

* Before purchasing equipment or durable goods, GRSOs should explore all resources available to them from the GA, the University Library, and other campus services and resources. All applications for equipment or durable goods expenditures should include a clear justification why existing resources are insufficient.

* GRSOs may apply for equipment, capital expenditures, or durable goods up to but not exceeding **$500 per round**. Durable goods include all items that can be reused for more than one event. This includes items such as tables, chairs, books, and other equipment.

## Nonprofit Donations {#nonprofit-donations}

* As a 501(c)(3) organization, the GA has a responsibility to ensure its funds are spent in accordance with its mission. While there are many worthwhile efforts and causes GRSOs may wish to support, GA funds must be used to support the UC Berkeley graduate community. Therefore, GA funds generally may not be used for donations or unconditional payments to other nonprofit organizations.

* This policy does not prevent GRSOs from paying for goods or services offered by nonprofit groups.

* In accordance with [Resolution 2105B](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fTQyNKdYhjiwIcLNMdK_rs2R6JfE2MyM0ZUlLo1W1Rc/edit#), the GA maintains a standing policy of providing support for the Native American community on campus and across California. The GA makes this commitment and undertakes these efforts on behalf of all student groups it represents and supports. As a result, individual GRSOs should not make individual donations or payments to Native land taxes such as the [Sogorea Te’ Shuumi Land Tax](https://sogoreate-landtrust.org/pay-the-shuumi-land-tax/), or similar unconditional contributions. GRSOs are encouraged to develop programming and events that support the Native community, but financial support is directed centrally by the GA. GRSOs should contact the Funding Officer and the Vice President of Equity and Inclusion for more details about how they can support and build upon the GA’s efforts to support Native students and all Native Californians.

# Use of Awarded Funds {#use-of-awarded-funds}

## Receiving Funds {#receiving-funds}

GRSOs who receive GA funds will have those funds credited to specially-created GA Funding CalLink accounts within a few days of the final decisions being announced. They can then make Purchase Requests to receive their reimbursements. They are responsible for their own Finance Agents. If you are working with a GRSO and are having difficulty getting your funds, we recommend you contact ASUC Finance at [asucfinance@berkeley.edu](mailto:asucfinance@berkeley.edu).

Individuals who receive Independent Organizer Funding or Professional Development or Graduate Parent Travel Awards will be added to a specific CalLink org, and can make Purchase Requests from that org to receive their reimbursements. These PRs are approved by the Funding Officer.

## Changing Events {#changing-events}

Any changes to events that have been allocated GA money need to be approved by the GA Funding Officer. This includes, but is not limited to, changes to event dates, speakers, venue, food costs, or supply costs. Please email the GA Funding Officer ASAP to receive approval for event changes at [funding@ga.berkeley.edu](mailto:funding@ga.berkeley.edu).

## Spending Unused Funds {#spending-unused-funds}

If you have leftover unused funds after your event, any requests to spend that leftover money need to be approved by the GA Funding Officer. Please email the GA Funding Officer ASAP to receive approval for event changes at [funding@ga.berkeley.edu](mailto:funding@ga.berkeley.edu). 

## Misuse of Funds {#misuse-of-funds}

If a GRSO is suspected of misusing GA funds, the Funding Officer or the Funding Committee may request proof of the GRSO’s GA sponsored events. Examples of misusing funds include using GA funds for purposes not approved by the Funding Officer or Committee, using GA funds in violation of the funding guide, or misrepresenting the number of student attendees to receive additional funding. This proof is required to ensure that GRSOs applying for large sums of GA money for large events are using the allocated funds as intended.

* This proof could be a sign-in sheet, a photo of the event, an RSVP list, or another form of reasonable proof that demonstrates the size of the event.

* The actual number of attendees does not need to exactly match the predicted number in the original application, but the predicted number and actual number of attendees should be reasonably close.

* If the GRSO does not submit this proof or does not provide a justification for why proof was not submitted or not possible to obtain, the Funding Committee has the discretion to fund any future applications from the GRSO fully, partially or not at all.

The Funding Committee has the discretion to internally audit any GRSO’s GA funding spending at any time.

# Frequently Asked Questions {#frequently-asked-questions}

For any questions or suggestions about GA Funding, please email [funding@ga.berkeley.edu](mailto:funding@ga.berkeley.edu). The Funding Officer can help navigate any of these application processes or set up a time to meet via Zoom or at the GA offices to go through applications, purchase requests, or other questions.

* Q: If I receive funding from several sources, can I submit one Purchase Request through CalLink to cover all costs?

  * A: No. You need to submit one request per funding source. 

* Q: If I have multiple purchases to reimburse from the same funding source, should I submit one Purchase Request?

  * A: Yes. Even if the purchases are for different events, you should combine them into one PR if they’re all for the same person.

* Q: Do I have to spend my funds on items that are in my budget?

  * A: Yes. See [Changing Events](#changing-events).

* Q: Is there a difference between GA funding and University funding?

  * A: Yes. They’re completely different and run by completely different people. We’ll do our best to point you to the right people if you have problems with University funding, but we can’t help you ourselves.

* Q: What if I don’t spend all my funds?

  * A: The GA does not hold accounts for groups, but allocates money to be used in the round that it is awarded. Once GRSO funds are allocated, the student organization is responsible for spending the allotted funds. Any funds approved in your application which are not used within the respective semester will not be rolled over to future semesters, but will instead be reclaimed at the end of the semester. The Professional Development Award and Graduate Parent Travel Award can be used up until the end of the academic year in which they were awarded.

* Q: How much money do I have left?

  * A: You can check on your org’s CalLink page. Click “Finance” and then “Accounts.”

* Q: Is a Purchase Order a payment?

  * A: No. A PO can be compared to a promissory note that has financial backing. The PO itself is not the actual payment. It is essentially an agreement to pay the vendor once the service/product is rendered. The estimated invoice is required to process the PO slip, which is a promise to pay the vendor given the estimated service charges. A final invoice must be submitted to ensure actual payment is made.

* Q: Can I be reimbursed in cash?

  * A: ASUC Finance only offers reimbursments via check or direct deposit. You can pick up checks in person at their window on the fourth floor of Eshleman Hall.

* Q: Does ASUC Finance accept credit card receipts alone?

  * A: ASUC Finance does not accept non-itemized credit card receipts. They cannot discern the purpose of claimed expenses when provided non-itemized receipts. You must turn in the original credit card receipt accompanied by the itemized receipt from the vendor. Both must be accurately dated and itemized, and include the company nam. All original receipts turned in must be clearly itemized by the company (not handwritten by a student group representative turning in the forms). If it is a register receipt, it must have the company name stamped on it.

* Q: Can a colleague pick up my reimbursement?

  * A: The individual who is receiving the reimbursement is the only person that is allowed to pick up the reimbursement regardless of who filled out the form. If the reimbursement is made to the group or vendor, only members whose names appear on the funding application may pick up the reimbursement.

* Q: What is the reimbursement policy for gas/mileage/transportation reimbursements?

  * A: Please include a full set of directions for mileage calculation. We will use [the current IRS-approved mileage rate](http://www.irs.gov/Tax-Professionals/Standard-Mileage-Rates) when using a personal car for travel.

* Q: What is the reimbursement policy for service tips reimbursements?

  * A: Tips have a suggested cap of 20% of the total bill. For service tips above 20%, please provide a written justification.
